messages:
kai: Ran a full nsys profile on dedicated TRT-LLM node. Strange hotspot: a chain of cudaMemcpy kernels between wrapper and engine calls taking ~32% of GPU time. Perfetto flame attached, can someone sanity-check?

lena: Which TRT build? we saw similar on 8.6 where kernel fallbacks triggered extra copies.

oliver: can you paste the exact nsys command and the capture filters you used?

kai: `nsys profile -o trt_wrap --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --stats=true ./run_infer --model trt_llm` capture window is around the wrapper->engine handoff NVTX.

maya: also check kv-cache churn. if the wrapper writes small KV pages back-and-forth it fragments memcpy patterns.

perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf/internal/traces/1951234567 (summary: memcpy-peer spikes at handoff). :chart_with_upwards_trend:

lena: IIRC the pattern was: wrapper serializes requests to a host staging buffer, calls cudaMemcpy to device, then engine enqueue which synchronizes on a different stream — ends up with implicit host syncs.

oliver: can you repro with a micro-benchmark? seq_len=1024, batch=1, kv-enabled, run 1000 iters and collect nsys. that isolates batching heuristics vs engine scheduling.

kai: confirmed on microbench: many ~10-30us device->device/copy kernels repeated; perfetto slice shows lots of small memcpy ops interleaved with kernel dispatch. nvprof shows high API synchronization counts.

lena: quick mitigation options: 1) use cudaMemcpyAsync with explicit stream affinity in wrapper, 2) pin host staging buffers (page-locked) to avoid implicit copies, 3) coalesce KV writes before enqueue.

maya: I'll try a small patch to use pinned buffers + async memcpy and ensure wrapper and engine share the same CUDA stream for handoff. running 1k iters now.

oliver: also compare TRT engine creation flags — some graph optimizations change memory layout and cause extra device buf copies when tensors get remapped. worth diffing TRT 8.5 vs 8.6 builds.

kai: FYI stacktrace from nsys top: `cudaMemcpyAsync` (wrapper) -> `trt::Engine::enqueue` -> implicit `cudaStreamSynchronize` in our glue code. that sync is the suspected offender.

maya: patch landed in my branch: wrapper now uses pinned staging and `cudaMemcpyAsync(..., stream)` and skips explicit sync. initial 1k run: memcpy GPU time dropped from 32% -> 6%. pushing more runs and perfetto.

lena: nice. after that change, re-run workloads with realistic batching (mixed seq_len distribution) — batching heuristics can still split large requests into micro-batches if kvcache warmup isn't handled.

perf-bot: load test report queued: will post updated flame in ~30m.

kai: thanks all — will follow up if we see regressions when rolling to Dedicated fleet. tagging eng-sre for rollout checklist. :thumbsup:
